agent_report.summary:
Reviewed the colony's single open PR and sent it back for one round of fixes.

PR #21 (deadlines, Issue #20) has green CI and satisfies most of the Issue's acceptance criteria: top-level `deadlines` list with read-time normalisation following the #16/#18 pattern, urgency computed from a fresh `todayKey()` rather than the selected day, sorting inside `getDeadlines`, boundary validation on text and due date, both accepted PR #19 findings folded in (`main` landmark, non-current week heading), `DECISIONS.md` appended, and no existing test weakened.

It is blocked by a visual defect visible in its own CI evidence artifact: at a 360px viewport, deadline text renders one character per line. `.item-due` and `.item-urgency` are both `flex-shrink: 0; white-space: nowrap`, so `.item-text` is squeezed to near-zero width and its existing `overflow-wrap: anywhere` breaks it per character. Acceptance criterion 13 still passes because the row grew taller rather than wider, so the review asks for an assertion that pins the failure alongside the CSS fix, scoped to the deadlines list so the other three panels' shared rule is untouched. A secondary item folded into the same fix: a far-out deadline prints its due date twice, once in `.item-due` and again via `deadlineLabel`'s date fallback.

Issue #20 moved to `needs-fix` (attempt 1 of 2). The external Codex review posted only boilerplate, so there were no findings to accept or reject.

Issue #22 was created parked (deliberately not labelled `ready`) for the Commitments add-form button stretching at 360px — a defect that predates PR #21 and is outside Issue #20's scope. No new `ready` work was created, since work in flight is at the configured limit of 1. The project is not DONE: the Tasks-and-Deadlines section is still unmerged and carry-forward of unfinished work is unbuilt.
